correctness.rationale: No core vertex can be selected, since an incident pendant leaf in the open neighborhood would have no neighbor outside the closed neighborhood. In a leaf-only selection, the open neighborhood is precisely the set of core vertices with a nonempty bundle. A partially selected bundle supplies its own outside neighbor; a fully selected bundle needs a core neighbor with no selected leaves. Partition by the uniquely determined zero-bundle set Z: the external boundary gets all nonempty selections and the undominated core vertices get only nonempty proper selections. This proves (1), including isolated vertices and the empty ESI set. At m=1 the proper-bundle factor vanishes, leaving exactly dominating Z and giving (2). At m≥2 each term has degree (m−1)n+|∂_H Z|−(m−1)|Z| and leading coefficient m^(n−|N_H[Z]|), with no cancellation, proving (3) and (4). For the classical identity used in (5), assign Roman labels 2 on Z, 0 on its exterior boundary and 1 elsewhere; conversely the zero-labeled vertices of any Roman function lie on the exterior boundary of its two-labeled set. Minimization gives γ_R=n−∂. The boundary is at most Δ|Z|, with equality for a singleton of maximum degree, so the claimed thresholds and m^n count follow. Independent adjacency-mask enumeration covered all 225 labeled-graph/multiplicity profiles of base orders 1–4 and m=1,2,3, testing 4,510,908 corona subsets and confirming the polynomials and extremal formulas. value.rationale: The formula counts all ESI sizes and extremal witnesses on a natural family built from arbitrary cores, including cores outside the earlier tree setting. Its single-leaf inversion encodes all base domination numbers by cardinality, not just the minimum, and the higher-m calculation separates baseline size from the count of optimal selections. These are concrete uses of the exact transform; no speedup or novelty of the old Roman identity is needed.
